@AustinScottGA08 @MorningsMaria @cherylcasone You can’t put lipstick on a pig and call it beautiful, increasing the deficit by 3.8 trillion dollars and giving big tax cuts to the wealthy isn’t worth the pitiful crumbs you tout for farmers

The One Big Beautiful Bill throws $60B at farm programs while slashing SNAP by $300B—classic D.C. shell game. Chairman Thompson claims to "strengthen the farm safety net," but gutting nutrition assistance for 3 million vulnerable Americans undermines food security. The bill prioritizes corporate tax breaks over working families, with 100% bonus depreciation for equipment purchases benefiting meatpackers more than small farmers.

While expanding livestock disaster relief and animal disease funding is smart, redirecting SNAP costs to states just shifts the burden instead of cutting bureaucratic bloat.

Real reform would audit USDA’s $160B annual budget to end subsidies for mega-corporations masquerading as "family farms."
